paragraphs: On Friday morning, Teacher Kim took her class to the school field. "Today we play a listening game," she said. "Mia is the leader, and you must follow her voice." Mia stood in front of the class with a small card in her hand. Lily, Leo, and May stood in a big circle. Pip sat next to Teacher Kim and watched. The morning was warm, and the grass was soft and green.

"Listen carefully," said Mia. She read each card slowly and waited a little after each one. "Put your hands up." "Clap two times." "Why is Leo clapping four times?" asked Mia. "Oh, I already clapped two times, but I did not stop," said Leo. "Turn to the left." "Jump three times." The other children did everything in the right order. Everybody laughed.

"Now keep your hands up," said Mia. "Change places with the child on your right." "Now meet in the middle of the circle." Lily and May walked to the middle, and Leo went the wrong way. "Stop, Leo!" said May. "You must listen to the voice." "My ears are terrible today," said Leo. "Then listen again," said Mia with a smile.

Then Teacher Kim gave Mia a new card. "This is the last card," said Mia. "Sit down. Close your eyes. Wait." The children sat on the grass and closed their eyes. Nobody moved, and the field was very quiet. Then they heard a small "Woof!" Pip was in the middle of the circle, and Leo opened one eye. "Open your eyes," said Mia. "You did very well." Teacher Kim smiled at Pip and said that he was the best listener of all.
